name: Airbus A300-600
summary: The first twin-engine widebody airliner (original A300 flew in 1972); the -600 is now flown in the US mainly as a freighter by FedEx and UPS.

wings: Low swept wing with small wingtip fences, no large winglets
engines: Two large turbofans (CF6-80C2 or PW4000) slung under the wings
fuselage: Fat widebody fuselage (wider than a 767) with a rounded, drooping nose
Freighters have no main-deck windows and a large cargo door forward on the left
tail: Tall, slightly swept fin with a low-set tailplane

tellTales: Fat widebody with only two engines and a rounded, drooping nose
Freighter variants lack passenger windows on the main deck
No big winglets, just small wingtip fences

confusedWith.howToTell: The A330 is longer, has larger engines and distinctive angled winglets; the A300 is shorter with only tiny wingtip fences.
The 767 is slimmer and many have tall blended winglets; the A300 has a fatter, rounder fuselage and only small wingtip fences.
The MD-11 has a third engine in the tail; the A300 has only two wing engines.
